app.name: Lectern

signIn.title: Sign in to Lectern
signIn.name: Name
signIn.noSignUp: There is no sign-up here. Whoever runs this Lectern adds people, and can give you a new password if you forgot yours.

account.thisComputer: Opened with this computer's link, which needs no password and works only here.
account.signOutFailed: Lectern didn't answer, so you are still signed in. Try again before you leave this browser to someone else.
account.passwordRule: At least 15 characters. A few words you'll remember work better than symbols.
account.differ: The two new passwords aren't the same.
account.changed: Your password is changed. Every other browser signed in as you has been signed out.

users.title: Users
users.adminOnly: Only an admin can add people or change their accounts.
users.notSetUp: Nobody signs in here yet: Lectern is opened with this computer's link. To let other people in, run `lectern user init <your name>` on the computer Lectern runs on. It asks for your password and makes you the admin; after that you add people here.
users.passwordSet: {{name}} has a new password and was signed out everywhere. Tell them the new one yourself: Lectern doesn't send it.
users.disabledWhy: A disabled account can't sign in. Its projects stay where they are.
users.name: Name
users.nameRule: 2 to 32 lower-case letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores. It is also the name of their folder, and can't be changed later.
users.passwordRule: At least 15 characters. It is shown as you type so you can pass it on; they can change it once they sign in.
users.makeAdmin: Admin: can add people, download and remove models, and change settings

below_minimum.name: Below minimum
below_minimum.summary: No usable GPU. Models run on the processor: it works, but slowly.

minimum.name: Minimum
minimum.summary: A 4B chat model. One model sits on the GPU at a time, so OCR and chat take turns.

recommended.name: Recommended
recommended.summary: A 9B chat model. OCR and chat swap on the GPU while a document is processed.

comfortable.name: Comfortable
comfortable.summary: Larger models, and chat and OCR can stay loaded together.

firstRun.title: Set up Lectern
firstRun.intro: Lectern runs every model on this computer. First, here's what it found, and the chat model that suits it.
firstRun.notYet: Setting it up downloads the models it runs on. Ask an admin to finish that, then check again.
firstRun.engineLlamaWhy: Runs every model. The chat is most reliable on it when it uses its tools.
firstRun.engineMlxWhy: Apple's own engine: faster replies, more mistakes when the chat uses its tools. Scanned pages still need llama.cpp and a small model to clean them up, both downloaded the first time you scan.
firstRun.engineStalled: No data for 30 seconds: the download seems stuck. After two minutes without any it stops, and you can try again.
firstRun.notEnoughDisk: There isn't enough free disk space for this model, plus 1 GB to spare. Free some space, then reload.
firstRun.sandboxFound: {{runtime}} {{version}} is running. Lectern will use it to run the scripts its models write, each in an isolated container.
firstRun.sandboxStopped: {{runtime}} is installed but not running. Start it so Lectern can run the scripts its models write.
firstRun.sandboxMissing: Neither Podman nor Docker is installed.
firstRun.sandboxWhy: Without one, Lectern can't run scripts, so answers that need exact numbers are marked not computed. Everything else works.
firstRun.sandboxGuide: How to install Podman or Docker

policy.mlx: Use MLX for MLX models (Apple Silicon)
policy.mlxMissing: MLX isn't installed with this Lectern, so every model runs on llama.cpp. The Mac installer adds it; from a checkout, run `uv sync --extra mlx` and start Lectern again.
policy.mlxWhy: MLX is Apple's own engine and can be faster on a Mac. Switched on, a model that has an MLX build runs on it: download the build under Models by role. A usual model already on disk goes on running until then. On MLX the chat makes more mistakes when it uses its tools. Scanned pages are still read and cleaned up on llama.cpp: cleaning one loads the model on the clean row beside the chat's.

webSearch.title: Web search
webSearch.enable: Let the chat search the web and open pages
webSearch.isOn: Web search is on: the chat can search the web and open pages.
webSearch.isOff: Web search is off: the chat answers from the project alone.
webSearch.what: The chat asks before each search, Wikipedia lookup or page it opens, and nothing is sent until you allow it. Searches go to {{hosts}}; a page is downloaded from its own site and saved in the project with its address.
webSearch.adminOnly: Only an admin can switch web search on or off. It applies to everyone on this Lectern.
webSearch.keyWhy: Optional. With a key, searches go to the Brave Search API first, which doesn't limit them the way DuckDuckGo and Yahoo do; those stay as the fallback. Get a key at brave.com/search/api. It is kept on this computer, readable by Lectern only, and never shown again.
webSearch.keyNone: No key: searches go to DuckDuckGo, then Yahoo.

projects.removeWhat: Its chats and OCR sessions stop, and its folder, with every file and scan in it, moves to the trash folder beside your projects folder, where its files can still be copied out. After 30 days it's deleted for good.
